This message comes from University at Buffalo, where scientists are working to protect the
Great Lakes and freshwater supplies around the world from harmful contamination.
Learn more about their research at buffalo.edu/npr.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
Oregon Governor Tina Kotek is thankful for the community member who stopped the gunman
who killed three children at a teacher and an elementary school in Bend from taking even
more lives.
No parent should have to have this kind of day.
And no community should have to live through this kind of day.
And as we learn more about the children and the adults who have been killed or injured
and their families and their loved ones, we are going to do a lot of crying and we are
going to cry together and we're probably going to cry privately.
Police described the gunman as a 16-year-old, an armed member of the community, saw the
suspect enter the school and pursued him.
Illinois authorities offering more detail about the 19-year-old suspect charged with
planning a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in suburban Chicago.
They say a car registered to the man entered the building's parking lot on Sunday, hours
before police arrested him after receiving a tip.
Vice President J.D.
Vance says Michigan voters face an existential choice in November.
It is a battle between those who loathe the United States of America and those who love
it, a battle between grievance and gratitude, between politicians obsessed with foreign
causes and leaders who remember that their first duty is to fight for the people right
here at home.
And speaking Thursday at a campaign rally in Monroe, Michigan, former Republican Congressman
Mike Rogers in a closely watched race against Democrat Abdullah Syed who spent Thursday
touring Michigan's upper peninsula with Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
I'm not supposed to run for office.
I know that.
Got the wrong name.
Apparently I pray the wrong way.
Wrong color skin.
But here's the thing about it.
How many of us have been told that we're not quite right?
The Democrats announced Wednesday that they will be increasing spending on behalf of Syed
in Michigan and Troy Jackson, who's running against Republican Senator Susan Collins in
Maine.
Parents may soon no longer have the option of buying their prescription drugs from Canadian
pharmacies to save money.
NPR Sydney Luckin reports on coming changes to import rules.
The U.S. allows people to import a 90-day supply of pharmaceuticals with a prescription
from a doctor under certain conditions.
And the medicines pass through customs fairly easily, as long as they are valued below $800.
But a rule change at U.S. Customs and Border Protection would require more paperwork, a
broker, and something called an entry bond.
That would make the practice more expensive or even impossible for the estimated 2 million
patients who import medicines for personal use.
The change was originally said to take effect next week, but has been pushed back to January
of next year.
Sydney Luckin, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Federal authorities are investigating letters containing suspicious substances that were
mailed to congressional and election offices around the country.
Authorities are urging recipients to treat the letters as potentially hazardous.
President Trump says the Pentagon will not live stream the execution of Fort Hood gunman
Nidal Malik Hassan.
In a social media post Thursday, Trump said that live streaming the execution might deter
terrorism, but he acknowledged that many prefer not to see it.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegcess' initial announcement of a public execution faced a backlash.
Milwaukee Brewers, heading to Major League Baseball's World Series for the first time
in more than 40 years.
The Brewers staged a comeback in Game 4 with Garrett Mitchell, hitting to go ahead home
run to beat Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4, and sweeping the best-of-seven National League
Championship Series in four games.
Reporter Steve Futterman was there.
The Dodger Dynasty comes to an end here in Los Angeles as the Milwaukee Brewers complete
a four-game sweep.
They win Game 4, 6-4.
They beat the Dodgers, four games to one.
It will be the Brewers going to their first World Series since 1982.
The Dodgers, the two-time defending champions, were hoping to make it a three-peat, becoming
the first team since the 2000 Yankees to win three in a row.
But they failed to make it even to the World Series.
The Dodgers are swept.
L.A.'s dynasty has come to an end.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles.
And I'm Giles Snyder.
This is NPR News.
